user.title: Connect Zigbee2MQTT
user.description: Zigbee Health reads the data Zigbee2MQTT already publishes via MQTT and analyses it. Nothing in your Zigbee network is changed.

data_description.base_topic: Base topic of your Zigbee2MQTT instance (default: zigbee2mqtt).
data_description.name: Shown in the device name, e.g. "Zigbee Health (Zigbee2MQTT)".

prerequisites.title: Recommended Zigbee2MQTT settings
prerequisites.description:
The following Zigbee2MQTT options are disabled: **{missing}**.

Without `last_seen`, Zigbee Health can only use the time it last received a message. Without `availability`, offline routers are only detected by the nightly network scan. Without `health`, the message counters for live traffic and message floods are missing.

**Easiest:** continue. After the first analysis (about 10 minutes, or right away with "Analyse now") the repairs dashboard shows one issue per option; "Submit" enables it in Zigbee2MQTT.

**Manually** in the Zigbee2MQTT frontend under Settings:
- `last_seen`: tab *Advanced* → *Last seen* → **ISO_8601**
- `availability`: tab *Availability* → **enable**
- `health`: tab *Health* → interval e.g. **10** minutes

room_without_router.title: Zigbee: no always-on router in {room}
room_without_router.description:
{room} has {count} battery devices but no router that is permanently on. Their radio messages have to travel far.

A Zigbee plug or another always-on router in this room makes the connection much more reliable.

too_few_routers.title: Zigbee: too few routers
too_few_routers.description:
{end_devices} battery devices share {routers} always-on routers. At most 8 devices per router and at least one router per floor are recommended.

Add about {recommended} more always-on routers (e.g. Zigbee plugs), spread over the rooms with the most battery devices.
